$comment: HAND-TRANSCRIBED. Higgsfield publishes prices as sentences, in three places: the "## Pricing" paragraph of a
route's console document (dash.higgsfield.ai/models/<id>/llms.txt), the price sentence its model page shows
beside its related models (open.higgsfield.ai/models/<id>/api-reference), and, once, the page description.
Every rate here is a human reading one of those sentences, which is why each row carries the exact `quote`,
the `source` URL and the date it was `verified`.
EVERY generation route has a row: a rate, or an `unpriced` reason. Silence stops codegen.
Row shape, a rate:
unit               per_image | per_second
usd                one rate, or one per value of `by` (keys are that field's WIRE values, verbatim)
by                 the wire field that selects the rate
byUnpublished      why no wire field selects it; `usd` is then keyed by the quote's own labels
usdWithVideoInput  the table that applies when any of `videoInputs` carries a clip
seconds            what a per-second rate multiplies: `request` (the body's `duration`), `source` (the clip at
`sourceParam`, with `rounding` as quoted and `maxSeconds` where a source states a trim, in
the quote or in `maxSecondsQuote`), `output` (the delivered clip, whose length the request
does not state) or `formula` (the quote's own arithmetic over durations the request does not
state)
count              a wire field the vendor says multiplies a per-image rate; `countQuote` is where it says so
multipliedBy       a field that changes how many images come back, where NO source says how it bills
catalog            the `by` value whose figure the catalog row's `cost` carries (owner decision, 2026-11-24, for
the Soul routes: the default resolution). Must be the default every source agrees on.
undefinedWhen      requests the quote prices in a way this row cannot express; no estimate is given there.
`changes: rate` also keeps the rate off the catalog row; `changes: unit` does not.
decided            the date the owner ruled that this rate is catalogued although the route's console document
says no price is public. Required on such a route, refused on any other.
…or an explicit non-price:
unpriced           the REASON no rate can be stated, in prose
THE CONSOLE'S "NO PUBLIC PRICING" SENTENCE. Where a route's page data has no pricing paragraph, its console
document prints "Public pricing information is not available for this model." under "## Pricing" — while the
model page, or the document's own description, states a price. Those are contradicting pages, and a rate read
off one of them is `unpriced` (the reason says so, and keeps the sentence as its `quote`) UNLESS the owner ruled
for that route: the row then carries `decided`, the date of the ruling, and its rate is published with the
caveat (`contradicted` on its rate, a CAVEAT line above its catalog row). Rulings so far: the three priced
Soul routes and AI Influencer, 2026-11-24.
Whether a route is contradicted is read off the snapshot, never entered by hand, and codegen stops on a rate
at a contradicted route without `decided`, and on a `decided` at a route that is not contradicted.
WHAT IS NOT A PRICE, and so is `unpriced`:
- a sample point. "$0.14 per second at 720p for 1 second clips" prices one combination of a resolution and
a clip length out of a range of lengths. A sentence is a rate TABLE only when what it qualifies its rates by
is one wire field's closed enum and it prices every member; codegen checks exactly that of every `by` row.
- a rate the vendor calls approximate ("Roughly costs …").
- token-metered pricing.
- a sentence the route's console document contradicts, where the owner has not ruled (see above).
TWO GUARDS, both run by scripts/codegen-higgsfield.ts on every generate:
A  every `quote`, `countQuote` and `maxSecondsQuote` must be a verbatim substring of that route's
committed snapshot (its console pricing paragraph, page price sentence, page description, a property
description or a docs usage note). A sentence that changed upstream therefore fails the refresh until
someone re-reads it.
B  every number in `usd` and `usdWithVideoInput` must be one of the dollar amounts in the row's own `quote`,
and, where the quote states an amount beside a key ("720p: $0.2647", "$0.054 each at 1k and 1.5k",
"for 6 second clips"), the amount under that key must be one the quote puts beside it. This catches a
transposed digit and two figures filed under each other's key.
A table may be keyed by any such field: Hailuo 2.3 prices its two `duration` values, 6 and 10, and offers no others.
A one-member `resolution` enum is written as a flat rate ("$0.035 each at 1k." on a route that offers only
`1k`), and so is a rate the quote states once for every value ("$0.015 each at 1k and 2k.").

kling-video/v4.0/video-edit.quote:
Standard self-serve rates in USD.

720p and 1080p are charged per second of output video:
- Without video input: 720p: $0.1257; 1080p: $0.1879.
- With video input: 720p: $0.1544; 1080p: $0.2336.
Input video duration is not added to the billed duration at these resolutions.

4K:
- Without video input: $0.549 × output duration in seconds.
- With video input: $0.329 × (output duration + max(total input video duration, output duration)), in seconds.
Input video duration includes reference videos and video-based elements after the 30-second trim.

HDR adds $0.047 per second of output video at 1080p or $0.078 at 4K, after base-price discounts, including fixed-price agreements. SDR has no additional charge.
